title: Clarifying the 'red books'
summary: He explains the red books were school military march books, not ragtime books.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Well I was going to ask, you mentioned these red books, is that the Redback Book of Rags?
No, the military march books. Marches, I didn't know. Yeah, the school kids get them a lot of times. Now I mean I think you get hold of a red book when you get to about the second or third grade
That's what I wanted to make clear on that. That's mostly military marches.
There had been some old ragtime books that Fess and all of them talk about calling the Redback Oh no, I wasn't referring to that.
I was talking about the school book, I mean the musical school, I mean the second grade of music you run into red books.
